$comment: General partnership agreement. Drafting only, jurisdiction-neutral: partnership statutes fill gaps differently everywhere, which is exactly why the agreement answers the big questions expressly instead of leaving them to whatever the local default happens to be. The wizard's founderNames answer supplies the partners; company is the partnership's name.

clauses.title: Formation and Name
clauses.rationale: A general partnership is created by the partners’ agreement to run a business together — this is that agreement saying so. A partnership takes at least two people; the signature block below carries every name from the wizard.
clauses.body: The undersigned (each a “Partner”, together the “Partners”) form a general partnership named {{company}} (the “Partnership”), effective {{date}}. The Partnership’s principal place of business is [address], and it may do business under other names the Partners approve.

clauses.title: Purpose
clauses.rationale: The purpose comes from the wizard in the user’s own words; keeping it specific bounds what any one partner can commit the others to.
clauses.body: The Partnership’s purpose is {{partnershipPurpose}}, and whatever is reasonably connected to it. Expanding into a materially different line of business requires the consent of all Partners.

clauses.title: Term
clauses.rationale: Open-ended until dissolved under this agreement — the alternative (a fixed term nobody remembers) creates accidental dissolutions.
clauses.body: The Partnership continues until it is dissolved as this Partnership Agreement provides. It does not end merely because a Partner leaves, if the remaining Partners choose to continue it under the section on a Partner’s departure.

clauses.title: Contributions
clauses.rationale: Money, property, and labor are all real contributions; listing them at signing is what makes the shares defensible later.
clauses.body: Each Partner contributes the following to the Partnership at signing: [Partner name — cash, property, or services, with an agreed value, for each Partner]. Additional contributions require the consent of all Partners, and no Partner is required to contribute more than what is listed.

clauses.title: Profit and Loss Shares
clauses.rationale: Equal shares is the starting text because it is the assumption most handshake partnerships already carry; the blank makes an unequal split a visible, deliberate edit.
clauses.body: Profits and losses are shared [equally among the Partners / as follows: [names and percentages, totalling 100%]]. Shares apply to profits and losses alike unless this section says otherwise.

clauses.title: Distributions and Draws
clauses.rationale: When money actually leaves the business is a different question from who owns it — and it is the question that starts most partner fights.
clauses.body: The Partners decide together when the Partnership distributes money, and distributions follow the profit shares. [Optional: each Partner may take a monthly draw of [amount] against their share, reviewed [quarterly].] The Partnership keeps reserves the Partners agree are prudent before distributing.

clauses.title: Books, Banking, and Records
clauses.rationale: Every partner can see the books, always — opacity between partners is where suspicion starts, and this clause makes transparency a right rather than a favor.
clauses.body: The Partnership keeps its money in its own bank account — not in any Partner’s personal account — and keeps accurate books. Every Partner may inspect the books and records at any reasonable time, without needing a reason. The Partnership’s accounting year is the calendar year, and [name] is responsible for keeping the records current.

clauses.title: Decisions
clauses.rationale: Two tiers: day-to-day decisions stay fast, big ones need everyone. The list of big ones is the substance — it is where partners disagree about what counts as big.
clauses.body: Ordinary day-to-day decisions may be made by any Partner. The following need the consent of all Partners: spending or borrowing over [amount]; hiring or firing; signing contracts longer than [12] months; admitting a new Partner; selling Partnership property outside the ordinary course; and anything outside the Partnership’s stated purpose.

clauses.title: Authority to Bind the Partnership
clauses.rationale: In a general partnership each partner can generally commit the others — which is why the internal limits, and the duty to make outsiders aware of them for big commitments, are worth writing down.
clauses.body: Each Partner may sign for the Partnership in the ordinary course of its business. For commitments that need all Partners’ consent under the Decisions section, a Partner will not sign until that consent exists in writing. A Partner who commits the Partnership in breach of this section is responsible to the other Partners for what it costs them.

clauses.title: Time and Outside Activities
clauses.rationale: Offered rather than automatic: some partnerships are everyone’s full-time job and some are side ventures, and pretending one default fits both would be a guess about the user’s situation.
clauses.body: Each Partner will devote [their full working time / approximately [number] hours per week] to the Partnership. A Partner may pursue other business activities that do not compete with the Partnership and do not use its property, information, or opportunities. Business opportunities within the Partnership’s purpose belong to the Partnership first.

clauses.title: Duties Between Partners
clauses.rationale: Partners owe each other honesty and fair dealing as a matter of the relationship itself; the clause states the standard the Partners are agreeing to hold each other to.
clauses.body: Each Partner will act honestly and in good faith toward the Partnership and the other Partners, account to the Partnership for any benefit taken from its business or property, and disclose conflicts of interest before acting on them.

clauses.title: Admitting a New Partner
clauses.rationale: Unanimous admission is the default that protects every existing partner — a partnership is personal, and nobody should acquire a partner they didn’t choose.
clauses.body: A new Partner may be admitted only with the written consent of all Partners, on terms (contribution, share, and any adjustments to existing shares) recorded in a signed amendment to this Partnership Agreement.

clauses.title: A Partner Leaving
clauses.rationale: The clause this document exists for. Without it, one person leaving can force the whole business to wind up; with it, the business survives the departure and the leaver gets paid out on known terms.
clauses.body: A Partner may leave the Partnership with at least [90] days’ written notice. The remaining Partners may continue the business, in which case the Partnership buys out the departing Partner’s interest at [an agreed valuation method — e.g. the value shown by the books plus that Partner’s share of the year’s profits to the departure date], paid [over [12] months / in a lump sum within [90] days]. The departing Partner remains responsible for obligations arising before departure and stops sharing in profits and losses from the departure date.

clauses.title: Death or Incapacity of a Partner
clauses.rationale: Offered because it is the conversation partners avoid and estates regret. The buyout mirrors the voluntary-departure terms so the estate is not negotiating from scratch while grieving.
clauses.body: If a Partner dies or becomes permanently unable to participate, the remaining Partners may continue the business, and the Partnership buys out that Partner’s interest on the same valuation and payment terms as a voluntary departure, paid to the Partner or their estate. The estate or representative does not become a Partner.

clauses.title: No Transfer of Partnership Interests
clauses.rationale: Keeps the partnership the same set of people its partners chose: interests can’t be sold or pledged to outsiders without everyone’s consent.
clauses.body: No Partner may sell, give away, or pledge any part of their Partnership interest without the written consent of all Partners. A purported transfer without consent gives the recipient no rights in the Partnership beyond receiving the transferring Partner’s distributions, if any.

clauses.title: Winding Up
clauses.rationale: The orderly ending: what gets paid in what order, and what happens to the name and the customers, decided while everyone is still on speaking terms.
clauses.body: The Partnership dissolves when all Partners agree in writing to end it, or when only one Partner remains and no continuation is agreed. On dissolution, the Partners wind up the business: assets are used first to pay the Partnership’s debts, then to return Partners’ unreturned contributions, and anything remaining is distributed by profit share. The Partners will agree in writing who, if anyone, may continue using the Partnership’s name and client relationships.

clauses.title: Deadlocks
clauses.rationale: Offered for even-numbered partnerships especially: when a required decision cannot be reached, the escalation path is the difference between a hard month and a dead company.
clauses.body: If the Partners cannot reach a decision this Partnership Agreement requires, any Partner may start the deadlock process: first a meeting of all Partners with [30] days to resolve it; then mediation with a mediator the Partners choose together; and if still unresolved after [60] more days, any Partner may invoke the departure or dissolution sections. No Partner may use a deadlock to force terms outside this agreement.
